### Regions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Regions")]

Santa Rosa County can be divided into three distinct sections: South Santa Rosa, Central Santa Rosa, and North Santa Rosa. The sections are centered on the main east–west roads that pass through the county.

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Navarre_Beach_Florida_sand.jpg/250px-Navarre_Beach_Florida_sand.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Navarre_Beach_Florida_sand.jpg)

[Navarre Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre_Beach,_Florida "Navarre Beach, Florida")

South Santa Rosa County comprises the area from Holley and Navarre in the east to Gulf Breeze]at the western end of the [Fairpoint Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairpoint_Peninsula "Fairpoint Peninsula"), and along [U.S. Highway 98](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_98_in_Florida "U.S. Route 98 in Florida"). A section of [Santa Rosa Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_Island,_Florida "Santa Rosa Island, Florida"), containing the unincorporated community of [Navarre Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre_Beach,_Florida "Navarre Beach, Florida"), is also part of South Santa Rosa County. Major bodies of water including [Santa Rosa Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_Sound "Santa Rosa Sound"), [Pensacola Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola_Bay "Pensacola Bay"), and [East Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bay_(Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida) "East Bay (Santa Rosa County, Florida)") strongly influence the housing and lifestyle of citizens in the southern part of the county. This fast-growing region serves primarily as "bedroom communities" for [Pensacola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola,_Florida "Pensacola, Florida") to the west and [Hurlburt Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurlburt_Field "Hurlburt Field"), [Fort Walton Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Walton_Beach,_Florida "Fort Walton Beach, Florida"), and [Eglin Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eglin_Air_Force_Base "Eglin Air Force Base") to the east.

Central Santa Rosa County is the area north of the bays and south of the extensive forests separating it from North Santa Rosa. The central section developed along the so-called [Old Spanish Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Spanish_Trail_(auto_trail) "Old Spanish Trail (auto trail)") that ran from [St. Augustine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Augustine,_Florida "St. Augustine, Florida") to [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans,_Louisiana "New Orleans, Louisiana"), and further points west. Today, [U.S. Highway 90](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_90_in_Florida "U.S. Route 90 in Florida") closely parallels the old trail, and is the main highway that connects the region. Despite recent growth, the Central Region is best identified by its rural roots, and can be best characterized by traditional [Southern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States "Southern United States") culture. The Pace and [Milton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton,_Florida "Milton, Florida") communities compose the Central Region, with both having populations roughly around 30,000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-9) The county seat, Milton is located where the trail crossed the [Blackwater River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackwater_River_(Florida) "Blackwater River (Florida)"). To the west of Milton bordering the Escambia River, Pace has experienced exponential growth, both residential and commercial. [Interstate 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_10_in_Florida "Interstate 10 in Florida") also passes through this section of the county. The [U.S. Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Navy "U.S. Navy") presence is marked by [Whiting Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Air_Station_Whiting_Field "Naval Air Station Whiting Field") and [NOLF Spencer Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Outlying_Landing_Field_Spencer "Naval Outlying Landing Field Spencer").

Northern Santa Rosa County is forest and farming country. The only town in the north is Jay. Most development has been along [State Road 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Road_4 "Florida State Road 4"), which runs through the northern sections of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and [Okaloosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okaloosa_County,_Florida "Okaloosa County, Florida") Counties. A large oil and natural gas field around Jay produced a great deal of oil, and made many farmers millionaires in the 1970s and 1980s, but the field has been depleted and is producing little oil today. The citizens have, for the most part, returned to farming and forestry for their livelihoods.

[State Road 87](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Road_87_(Florida) "State Road 87 (Florida)") traverses the county from north to south, between U.S. Highway 98 and the border with [Escambia County, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escambia_County,_Alabama "Escambia County, Alabama"), near [Brewton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brewton,_Alabama "Brewton, Alabama"), where it connects with [State Route 41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Route_41_(Alabama) "State Route 41 (Alabama)"). This road is a primary [emergency evacuation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_evacuation "Emergency evacuation") route for the county during [hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricanes "Hurricanes").

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Government")]

### Board of county commissioners

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Board of county commissioners")]

The Santa Rosa County Board of County Commissioners serves as the legislative and policy-setting body of the county as established under Section 125 of the Florida Statutes. As such, the board enacts all legislation and authorizes programs and expenditures within the county. The board appoints a professionally trained county administrator, who is responsible for policy and budget development and implementation.

The board comprises five members, elected countywide. Members must reside within the particular districts for which they seek election. Each year, the board organizes itself, selecting a chair and vice chair from among its members to preside at commission meetings.

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), 188,000 people, 69,454 households, and 47,876 families resided in the county.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)

The median age was 40.3 years; 22.8% of residents were under the age of 18 and 16.7% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 103.1 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 102.1 males age 18 and over.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

The racial makeup of the county was 80.4% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Americans "White Americans"), 5.9% [Black or African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans"), 0.7% [American Indian and Alaska Native](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States"), 2.1% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Americans "Asian Americans"), 0.2% [Native Hawaiian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Hawaiians "Native Hawaiians") and [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander "Pacific Islander"), 1.9% from some other race, and 8.8% from [two or more races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial_Americans "Multiracial Americans"). [Hispanic or Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") residents of any race comprised 6.3% of the population.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)

80.1% of residents lived in urban areas, while 19.9% lived in rural areas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DHC-27)

Of the 69,454 households, 32.8% had children under the age of 18 living in them; 56.6% were married-couple households, 15.2% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 22.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 21.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 9.6% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

There were 75,854 housing units, of which 8.4% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 77.3% were owner-occupied and 22.7% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.4% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.5%.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [2000 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_census "2000 United States census"),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR8-28) 117,743 people, 43,793 households, and 33,326 families resided in the county. The population density was 116 inhabitants per square mile (45/km 2). The 49,119 housing units had an average density of 48 per square mile (19/km 2). The [racial makeup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)") of the county was 90.72% White, 4.25% African American, 1.01% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 1.30% Asian, 0.08% Pacific Islander, 0.67% from other races, and 1.98% from two or more races. About 2.52% of the population were Hispanics or Latinos of any race.

Of the 43,793 households, 36.5% had children under 18 living with them, 62.2% were married couples living together, 10.2% had a female householder with no husband present, and 23.9% were not families. About 19.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 6.6% had someone living alone who was 65 or older. The average household size was 2.63 and the average family size was 3.00.

In the county, the age distribution was 26.6% under 18, 7.2% from 18 to 24, 31.1% from 25 to 44, 24.1% from 45 to 64, and 11.0% who were 65 or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 100.6 males. For every 100 females 18 and over, there were 97.9 males.

The median income for a household in the county was $41,881 and for a family was $46,929. Males had a median income of $34,878 versus $22,304 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the county was $20,089. About 7.9% of families and 9.8% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 12.6% of those under 18 and 7.5% of those 65 or over.

## Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Politics")]

Santa Rosa County is a stronghold of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"). It has supported the Republican candidate in each presidential election since [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_United_States_presidential_election "1972 United States presidential election"), consistently by overwhelming margins.

**Santa Rosa County** is a [county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(United_States) "County (United States)") in the northwestern portion of the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida"). As of 2020, its population was 188,000. The [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") is [Milton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton,_Florida "Milton, Florida"), which lies in the geographic center of the county. Other major communities within Santa Rosa County are [Navarre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida "Navarre, Florida"), [Pace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pace,_Florida "Pace, Florida"), and [Gulf Breeze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Breeze "Gulf Breeze").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR6-1) Navarre is the most populated community, with a population of approximately 45,000 residents. Santa Rosa County is included in the [Pensacola metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola_metropolitan_area "Pensacola metropolitan area"), which also includes [Escambia County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escambia_County,_Florida "Escambia County, Florida").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first European in Santa Rosa County may have been Diego Maldonado, a member of [Tristan de Luna's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trist%C3%A1n_de_Luna_y_Arellano "Tristán de Luna y Arellano") failed expedition. Natives dominated the area until the late 1700s. A [Spanish mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_missions_in_Florida "Spanish missions in Florida") serving [Apalachees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apalachee "Apalachee"), Nuestra Señora de la Soledad y San Luís, may have been located in [Floridatown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floridatown,_Florida "Floridatown, Florida") from 1718 until 1740.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-3)

Santa Rosa County was created in 1842, when it was divided from Escambia County. It was named after the barrier island along its southern coast, which, in turn, had been named for the Roman Catholic saint [Rosa de Viterbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosa_de_Viterbo "Rosa de Viterbo").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-4)

Santa Rosa County repealed its prohibition on alcohol in 2005.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-5)

Santa Rosa County has seen unprecedented growth in population, specifically in [Navarre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida "Navarre, Florida"), [Pace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pace,_Florida "Pace, Florida"), and [Gulf Breeze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Breeze,_Florida "Gulf Breeze, Florida"). The county is a quickly growing tourist destination because of its access to beaches and protected wilderness areas for kayaking, hiking, and camping.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-6)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

### Regions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Regions")]

Santa Rosa County can be divided into three distinct sections: South Santa Rosa, Central Santa Rosa, and North Santa Rosa. The sections are centered on the main east–west roads that pass through the county.

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Navarre_Beach_Florida_sand.jpg/250px-Navarre_Beach_Florida_sand.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Navarre_Beach_Florida_sand.jpg)

[Navarre Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre_Beach,_Florida "Navarre Beach, Florida")

South Santa Rosa County comprises the area from Holley and Navarre in the east to Gulf Breeze]at the western end of the [Fairpoint Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairpoint_Peninsula "Fairpoint Peninsula"), and along [U.S. Highway 98](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_98_in_Florida "U.S. Route 98 in Florida"). A section of [Santa Rosa Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_Island,_Florida "Santa Rosa Island, Florida"), containing the unincorporated community of [Navarre Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre_Beach,_Florida "Navarre Beach, Florida"), is also part of South Santa Rosa County. Major bodies of water including [Santa Rosa Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_Sound "Santa Rosa Sound"), [Pensacola Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola_Bay "Pensacola Bay"), and [East Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bay_(Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida) "East Bay (Santa Rosa County, Florida)") strongly influence the housing and lifestyle of citizens in the southern part of the county. This fast-growing region serves primarily as "bedroom communities" for [Pensacola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola,_Florida "Pensacola, Florida") to the west and [Hurlburt Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurlburt_Field "Hurlburt Field"), [Fort Walton Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Walton_Beach,_Florida "Fort Walton Beach, Florida"), and [Eglin Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eglin_Air_Force_Base "Eglin Air Force Base") to the east.

Central Santa Rosa County is the area north of the bays and south of the extensive forests separating it from North Santa Rosa. The central section developed along the so-called [Old Spanish Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Spanish_Trail_(auto_trail) "Old Spanish Trail (auto trail)") that ran from [St. Augustine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Augustine,_Florida "St. Augustine, Florida") to [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans,_Louisiana "New Orleans, Louisiana"), and further points west. Today, [U.S. Highway 90](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_90_in_Florida "U.S. Route 90 in Florida") closely parallels the old trail, and is the main highway that connects the region. Despite recent growth, the Central Region is best identified by its rural roots, and can be best characterized by traditional [Southern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States "Southern United States") culture. The Pace and [Milton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton,_Florida "Milton, Florida") communities compose the Central Region, with both having populations roughly around 30,000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-9) The county seat, Milton is located where the trail crossed the [Blackwater River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackwater_River_(Florida) "Blackwater River (Florida)"). To the west of Milton bordering the Escambia River, Pace has experienced exponential growth, both residential and commercial. [Interstate 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_10_in_Florida "Interstate 10 in Florida") also passes through this section of the county. The [U.S. Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Navy "U.S. Navy") presence is marked by [Whiting Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Air_Station_Whiting_Field "Naval Air Station Whiting Field") and [NOLF Spencer Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Outlying_Landing_Field_Spencer "Naval Outlying Landing Field Spencer").

Northern Santa Rosa County is forest and farming country. The only town in the north is Jay. Most development has been along [State Road 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Road_4 "Florida State Road 4"), which runs through the northern sections of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and [Okaloosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okaloosa_County,_Florida "Okaloosa County, Florida") Counties. A large oil and natural gas field around Jay produced a great deal of oil, and made many farmers millionaires in the 1970s and 1980s, but the field has been depleted and is producing little oil today. The citizens have, for the most part, returned to farming and forestry for their livelihoods.

[State Road 87](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Road_87_(Florida) "State Road 87 (Florida)") traverses the county from north to south, between U.S. Highway 98 and the border with [Escambia County, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escambia_County,_Alabama "Escambia County, Alabama"), near [Brewton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brewton,_Alabama "Brewton, Alabama"), where it connects with [State Route 41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Route_41_(Alabama) "State Route 41 (Alabama)"). This road is a primary [emergency evacuation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_evacuation "Emergency evacuation") route for the county during [hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricanes "Hurricanes").

### Board of county commissioners

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Board of county commissioners")]

The Santa Rosa County Board of County Commissioners serves as the legislative and policy-setting body of the county as established under Section 125 of the Florida Statutes. As such, the board enacts all legislation and authorizes programs and expenditures within the county. The board appoints a professionally trained county administrator, who is responsible for policy and budget development and implementation.

The board comprises five members, elected countywide. Members must reside within the particular districts for which they seek election. Each year, the board organizes itself, selecting a chair and vice chair from among its members to preside at commission meetings.

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), 188,000 people, 69,454 households, and 47,876 families resided in the county.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)

The median age was 40.3 years; 22.8% of residents were under the age of 18 and 16.7% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 103.1 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 102.1 males age 18 and over.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

The racial makeup of the county was 80.4% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Americans "White Americans"), 5.9% [Black or African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans"), 0.7% [American Indian and Alaska Native](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States"), 2.1% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Americans "Asian Americans"), 0.2% [Native Hawaiian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Hawaiians "Native Hawaiians") and [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander "Pacific Islander"), 1.9% from some other race, and 8.8% from [two or more races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial_Americans "Multiracial Americans"). [Hispanic or Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") residents of any race comprised 6.3% of the population.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)

80.1% of residents lived in urban areas, while 19.9% lived in rural areas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DHC-27)

Of the 69,454 households, 32.8% had children under the age of 18 living in them; 56.6% were married-couple households, 15.2% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 22.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 21.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 9.6% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

There were 75,854 housing units, of which 8.4% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 77.3% were owner-occupied and 22.7% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.4% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.5%.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [2000 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_census "2000 United States census"),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR8-28) 117,743 people, 43,793 households, and 33,326 families resided in the county. The population density was 116 inhabitants per square mile (45/km 2). The 49,119 housing units had an average density of 48 per square mile (19/km 2). The [racial makeup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)") of the county was 90.72% White, 4.25% African American, 1.01% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 1.30% Asian, 0.08% Pacific Islander, 0.67% from other races, and 1.98% from two or more races. About 2.52% of the population were Hispanics or Latinos of any race.

Of the 43,793 households, 36.5% had children under 18 living with them, 62.2% were married couples living together, 10.2% had a female householder with no husband present, and 23.9% were not families. About 19.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 6.6% had someone living alone who was 65 or older. The average household size was 2.63 and the average family size was 3.00.

In the county, the age distribution was 26.6% under 18, 7.2% from 18 to 24, 31.1% from 25 to 44, 24.1% from 45 to 64, and 11.0% who were 65 or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 100.6 males. For every 100 females 18 and over, there were 97.9 males.

The median income for a household in the county was $41,881 and for a family was $46,929. Males had a median income of $34,878 versus $22,304 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the county was $20,089. About 7.9% of families and 9.8% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 12.6% of those under 18 and 7.5% of those 65 or over.

Summary

Navarre is a city in Florida, the United States. The population in Navarre was 39,838 in 2024. The median age in Navarre was 38.8 in 2024. The median income in Navarre was $49,916 in 2024. The percentage of people with obesity in Navarre was 30.9% in 2022. The percentage of people who binge drink in Navarre was 19.8% in 2022. The percentage of people who smoke in Navarre was 13.7% in 2022.

**Navarre** is a [census-designated place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census-designated_place "Census-designated place") and [unincorporated community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unincorporated_area#United_States "Unincorporated area") in Santa Rosa County in the northwest [Florida Panhandle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Panhandle "Florida Panhandle"). It is a major [bedroom community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commuter_town "Commuter town") for mostly [U.S. military personnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Armed_Forces "United States Armed Forces"), [federal civil servants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_federal_civil_service "United States federal civil service"), local population, retirees and defense contractors. Due to Navarre Beach and the 4 miles (6.4 km) of beach front on the [Gulf of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico") thereof, as well as several miles of beaches within the [Navarre Beach Marine Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre_Beach_Marine_Park "Navarre Beach Marine Park") and the [Gulf Islands National Seashore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Islands_National_Seashore "Gulf Islands National Seashore"), it has a small, but rapidly growing community of nature enthusiasts and tourists.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:10-4) Navarre has grown from being a small town of around 1,500 in 1970 to a town with a population estimated at 43,540 as of 2022[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit), if including both the Navarre and Navarre Beach [Census Designated Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census_Designated_Place "Census Designated Place").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-Navarre_Census-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-NB_Census-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:26-7) The Navarre CDP recorded a population of 40,817 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-8)

Navarre is about 25 miles (40 km) east of [Pensacola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola,_Florida "Pensacola, Florida") and about 15 miles (24 km) west of [Fort Walton Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Walton_Beach,_Florida "Fort Walton Beach, Florida"). The community is roughly centered on the junction of [U.S. Route 98](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_98_in_Florida "U.S. Route 98 in Florida") and [State Road 87](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Road_87 "Florida State Road 87").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-towncenter-plan-9) It is part of the [Pensacola–Ferry Pass–Brent, Florida Metropolitan Statistical Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola_metropolitan_area "Pensacola metropolitan area") (more commonly referred to as the Pensacola Metro Area), and is the second largest community in the metropolitan area, according to a study.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:3-10) Navarre is the third-largest community in the [Florida Panhandle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Panhandle "Florida Panhandle").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:3-10)

Navarre is the principal community of the census-defined [Navarre-Miramar Beach-Destin Urbanized Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_urbanized_areas_in_Florida_(by_population) "List of urbanized areas in Florida (by population)"). The community is known for the natural environment, swimming, picnic spots, and its beach.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:10-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/NavarreBeachonabusyday.jpg/250px-NavarreBeachonabusyday.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NavarreBeachonabusyday.jpg)

A busy day on Navarre Beach

### Early Exploration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early Exploration")]

In 1693, Spanish explorers [Carlos de Sigüenza y Góngora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_de_Sig%C3%BCenza_y_G%C3%B3ngora "Carlos de Sigüenza y Góngora") and Admiral Andrés de Pez y Malzárraga became the first recorded Europeans to explore what is, today, Navarre. Sigüenza was responsible for scouting and mapping possible sites of Spanish colonization in [Northwest Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Florida "Northwest Florida") during the expedition. While traveling in the area of [East Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bay_(Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida) "East Bay (Santa Rosa County, Florida)") in April 1693 the Spanish discovered what is today called the [East Bay River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bay_River "East Bay River").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) In honor of Captain Jordan de Reina, an officer serving in the expedition, the Spanish dubbed the waters on which they traveled, "The River Jordan".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)

On April 11, 1693, while sailing up East Bay River, sailors aboard the Spanish ships noticed a group of Native Americans observing from a camp near the shore. In order to greet the natives, a landing party was sent out. By the time the Spanish reached the shore, however, the Native Americans were gone. As the Natives quickly abandoned camp the Spanish discovered half-cooked pieces of buffalo meat sitting over a fire, along with a fierce dog guarding the site. Due to the great number of oak trees in the area the campsite was named "El Robledal," meaning "The Oakgrove" in Spanish. Neighborhoods in the area of this event still retain the El Robledal name. [[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) After erecting a wooden cross and leaving gifts for the natives, the Spaniards continued their exploration upriver. Upon later return to El Robledal, the explorers noticed that their gifts had been taken. In return, the natives had also constructed a wooden cross and left a buffalo hide as a peace offering. The earliest known map of Robledal dates from 1693, the same year as the Pez-Sigüenza Expedition. Subsequent maps in 1698 continue to note the area today known as Navarre as Robledal.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)

### Axelson Point and early settlement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Axelson Point and early settlement")]

#### Settlement and shipyard

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Settlement and shipyard")]

White settlers are noted as living in the area since at least 1827, when a map of West Florida includes listings of families by the name of Wyman and Williams living along [Santa Rosa Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_Sound "Santa Rosa Sound") in what would become Navarre. The Wyman family is believed to be related to [Guy Wyman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Wyman "Guy Wyman"), who, along with his wife, would name the area "Navarre" and is now generally recognized as the town founder. The Williams family is likely the source of the name of [William's Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William's_Creek "William's Creek").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-13)

While various settlers had been present in the area since before this time, Robledal was again populated sometime near 1856, with the establishment of a [homestead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homestead_Acts "Homestead Acts") by the Axelson Family.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) Due to the relative lack of information on the other families, as well as their homestead's location at Robledal, they are often considered Navarre's first settlers. Their home was along the shore of the East Bay, on a small [cape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_(geography) "Cape (geography)"), in which, they are now the namesake, after the point was officially designated, [Axelson Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axelson_Point "Axelson Point").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-15)

Soon after their settlement in what would become Navarre, they established a shipyard on Axelson Point, jutting into what was also then called, Axelson Cove.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12) The shipyard was considered to be mostly successful, as the family made a business of fixing ships in port in the nearby deep-water port in [Pensacola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola,_Florida "Pensacola, Florida") and the river port in [Milton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton,_Florida "Milton, Florida"), as well as building large-scale ships of their own.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) The shipyard was in operation until approximately 1890.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)

#### Civil War

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Civil War")]

During the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War"), despite the political ideology of citizens in the local area,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:17-16) records make it seem as though the Axelson's were pro-union. This is substantiated by a record showing that, while many businesses in the area were becoming ruined due to the [Union blockade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_blockade "Union blockade") of southern ports, the Axelson's shipyard was quite busy and prosperous, primarily from business completed with the [Union navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Navy "Union Navy") and the [United States Merchant Marines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Merchant_Marine "United States Merchant Marine").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:13-11) This notion is conflicted with local tradition noted in _Log of the Peep O'Day_, an account of the area from the 1910s, which suggest that the Axelsons built one of the first ships [registered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_registration "Ship registration") under the flag of the [Confederacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederate_States_of_America "Confederate States of America").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) However, as confirmed by evidence gathered by historians at the [University of West Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_West_Florida "University of West Florida"), this notion was likely caused by a confusion between the Axelsons and shipbuilding operations in nearby [Milton, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton,_Florida "Milton, Florida").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14)

In addition, some records and books, such as the _Atlas of Florida_, attest that Union raids were made against [Confederate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederate_States_of_America "Confederate States of America") troops and camps stationed elsewhere in [Northwest Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Florida "Northwest Florida"), through routes in what would become Navarre and [Holley, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holley,_Florida "Holley, Florida").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-18) No evidence exists that the Axelsons assisted such missions. A military road that appears to approximate this route is noted as existing as late as 1895, where it can be found on [War Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_War "United States Department of War") maps from that time period.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-19)

#### Bilowry and Hiawatha

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Bilowry and Hiawatha")]

Some maps of the area during this time, seem to indicate that the area was also known as “Bilowry,” a presumed misspelling or combination of the name, Bill Lowry.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:17-16) The area also had a post office under this name from 1886 to 1891.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-21)

Habitation of this area of what is now Navarre was continuous, though sparse from the Axelsons to the platting of Navarre.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:16-14) This area also came to be known as Hiawatha during a brief time, with a neighborhood in Navarre still retaining this name.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-23)

### Town of Eagan

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Town of Eagan")]

Some 30 years after the first homestead in the area was established, seemingly coinciding with the community of Bilowry, a small settlement named Eagan arose in 1874.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:14-12)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-24) The post office was run by Patrick Shea, a naturalized American from Ireland.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) The settlement, composed of approximately 40 families, was located off the Santa Rosa Sound and encompassed a portion of present-day Navarre. The settlement, which formerly existed as a post office location, was named after a local postmaster, John Eagan Esq., a Pensacola lawyer and politician.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) Following the post office's discontinuation on September 11, 1884, families continued to live in the area, and the town continued to appear on area maps even into the 1890s.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25) While what became of the town and the people who lived there at that time is unknown (some of which are known to have remained in the town, some of which are believed to have moved to neighboring communities), the discovery of the town's existence definitively established the settlement of the Navarre area in South Santa Rosa County as being prior to the 20th century. The land upon which Eagan existed would, in fact, later become what is now known as Navarre.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:24-25)

### Guy Wyman and town development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Guy Wyman and town development")]

The founder of Navarre, under the name of Navarre, was [Guy Wyman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Wyman "Guy Wyman"), a colonel in the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army"). During [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"), he met a [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") nurse named Noelle. At the time, immigration policies would not allow him to bring her to the United States as a fiancée or even as a wife, but he could bring her back as his legal child. Colonel Wyman, therefore, adopted her and brought her back to the Florida panhandle, where he purchased a large amount of land. Noelle named their holdings _Navarre_, after the [province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre "Navarre") in [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain"), near France.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-towncenter-plan-9)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-26) Wyman [platted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plat "Plat") the town in 1925,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-towncenter-plan-9) but made no steps towards development. However, during the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression"), the Wymans could not pay the taxes on it and were forced to begin selling it off. Part of that property is where the Navarre Park is today.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-27)

Navarre appeared with its modern name, though spelled _Neverre_, on a 1926 region map created by the [Louisville and Nashville Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_and_Nashville_Railroad "Louisville and Nashville Railroad").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-28)

Gary Roberts, a nephew of founder Guy Wyman, helped to develop the town even further from 1933 to his death in 1941. Roberts created a path from his home in Navarre to his timber yard in [Holley, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holley,_Florida "Holley, Florida"). This portion of road later become a part of [Florida State Road 87](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Road_87 "Florida State Road 87").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Modern era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Modern era")]

Most of the scenes in _[Jaws 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaws\_2 "Jaws 2")_ were filmed in and around Navarre and Navarre Beach in 1977.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-30) The production "was a boost to the local economy because local boaters, extras and stand-ins or doubles were hired."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:9-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-32)

In the 21st Century, Navarre has become one of the fastest-growing communities in Florida. While protecting and enhancing the natural environment of the area; many steps have been taken to develop luxury accommodations, water activities, boutique shopping, scenic trails, schools and nature/educational opportunities.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-34)

#### Hurricanes Ivan and Dennis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Hurricanes Ivan and Dennis")]

Navarre has been impacted significantly by hurricanes.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:18-35) Immediately preceding [Hurricane Ivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ivan "Hurricane Ivan") and [Hurricane Dennis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dennis "Hurricane Dennis"), Navarre was seeing a new strand of growth and economic advancement. This, however, quickly came to a close, as Navarre suffered horribly during the events of those hurricanes. Many planned developments stopped and decided to delay their plans until a later date, many of which were never resumed or completed. This hard mark against Navarre lingered until the mid and late 2010s.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:18-35)

#### Helicopter crash

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Helicopter crash")]

On March 10, 2015, a [UH-60](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikorsky_UH-60_Black_Hawk "Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk"), call sign MOJO 69, from the Louisiana National Guard, crashed in the Santa Rosa Sound off the coast of the community of Navarre. All eleven on board were believed killed.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-36) On November 18, 2016, Leadership Santa Rosa Class 29 unveiled the Navarre Black Hawk Memorial in Navarre Park. The memorial was built to honor the men who died in the Black Hawk crash and anyone who has paid the ultimate sacrifice in service to the United States.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-37)

#### Protests

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Protests")]

2017 and 2018 had seen a noticeable rise in civil activism in the Navarre area, with three notable protests occurring, all within the span of 12 months.

The first protests recorded in the community occurred on June 9, 2017,[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:4-38) after the county unilaterally changed the town's nickname and locally popular welcome sign. The change was made without the consent of the citizens of the town[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:5-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:7-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:8-41) and have sparked additional calls for the incorporation of the community as a municipality.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:4-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:5-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:7-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:8-41)

In 2018, there were protests against the Holley-Navarre Water System.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:0-42) The protests were over the water system's potential violations of the [Florida Sunshine Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Sunshine_Law "Florida Sunshine Law"), which guarantees the rights for citizens and residents to access the meetings and public records of government agencies. The alleged violations occurred when the board of directors of the agency met for what they called a "secret" meeting. The board president stated these meetings were closed due to their nature of discussing legal matters between members of the board and of several [attorneys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attorney_at_law "Attorney at law") and lawyers.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:0-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:6-43) A new board was later elected, largely defusing the situation.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:6-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-45) The water system has subsequently received criticism after the new water board appointed a former [Santa Rosa County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County "Santa Rosa County")[commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_commissioner "County commissioner") who had just been voted out of his seat a month before his hiring.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-48) A later CEO of the water system was dismissed after undisclosed felony charges were discovered.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-50)

The third notable protests were part of the larger national school walkout to promote gun control.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:2-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-52)

On June 3, 2020, there was a protest at Navarre Park as part of the [George Floyd protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests"). It consisted of around 120 protestors and was followed by a candlelight vigil at the main pavilion of the park.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-53)

#### Growth and incorporation efforts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Growth and incorporation efforts")]

For the first time since before hurricanes Ivan and Dennis, Navarre is now not only expanding in population, but in attractions, dining establishments, and other tourist options as well. In the late 2010s, Navarre saw the construction and opening of several major housing and apartment complexes, a brand new hotel, retail stores, several new restaurants and Santa Rosa County's first microbrewery.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-56) Expansion has since continued with the construction of additional retail and box stores, residential complexes, and entertainment centers near the community's central business district.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-59) New development was announced in 2020 that would additionally expand commercial options on the east side of the community.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-60)

In 2020, following a failed effort in 2014, a new effort in incorporating has been established by a local [political action committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_action_committee "Political action committee"), the Navarre Area United PAC.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-63) However, the PAC was delayed in collecting petition signatories to get the issue of incorporation on the ballot due to the [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") outbreak. They had been expected to resume collecting signatures after the pandemic, but had been delayed by stalling from local legislators.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-66) Continuing the cause in 2021, the Preserve Navarre campaign began to conduct research regarding the feasibility of Navarre incorporation. Therefore, once again possibly reviving the political question for the future.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-67) The latter group since released a feasibility study (later updated according to local feedback) and a proposed charter.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:26-7)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-68) In October 2024, a quickly organized straw poll organized by the committee through a private election firm failed to reach 50% approval of voters.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:20-70) While concerns, including a small turnout, continued regarding whether the poll adequately demonstrated the community's opinion on the proposal, the organization dropped the effort.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:20-70)

In May 2023, the Highway 98 widening project has begun in select areas of Navarre, specifically east of Highway 87. The project consists of drainage improvements, sidewalks, and adding 3 lanes to both eastbound and westbound lanes. While the end date has not been announced, it is expected to be finished in the 2026/27 timeframe.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Location")]

Navarre is located on roughly 12 miles (19 km) of shoreline along the [Gulf of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-72)

### Topography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Topography")]

The community of Navarre is located on the [Gulf Coastal Plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Coastal_Plain "Gulf Coastal Plain") and is built on mostly flat sandy soil, though there are a few shallow hills. Navarre is primarily located on the [Fairpoint Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairpoint_Peninsula "Fairpoint Peninsula") and [Santa Rosa Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_Island_(Florida) "Santa Rosa Island (Florida)"). Navarre is bounded geographically in the north by the East Bay River, the [Yellow River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_River_(Pensacola_Bay) "Yellow River (Pensacola Bay)"), and several [creeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stream "Stream") and on the south by the Santa Rosa Sound.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-towncenter-plan-9) Holley, a different census-designated place that is sometimes considered part of Navarre, is north of the Fairpoint Peninsula, across the [East Bay River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bay_River "East Bay River").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-73)

#### Hurricanes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Hurricanes")]

As a low-elevation community near the Gulf of Mexico, Navarre is often threatened by hurricanes. Significant damage was incurred as a result of hurricanes [Erin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Erin_(1995) "Hurricane Erin (1995)") and [Opal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Opal "Hurricane Opal") in 1995, Georges in 1998, Ivan in 2004, Dennis in 2005 and Sally in 2020. Many homes and businesses immediately along Santa Rosa Sound (generally south of [U.S. Highway 98](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Highway_98 "U.S. Highway 98")) suffered [storm surge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storm_surge "Storm surge") as a result of those storms. Recoveries have been rendered by the area with the population quickly [flourishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flourishing "Flourishing"). This area of Florida is consistently listed as one of the worst places for hurricanes.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-75)

### Navarre Beach

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Navarre Beach")]

Navarre Beach is the beach neighborhood of Navarre and is, as of the 2010 census, its own census designated place. It is on [Santa Rosa Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_Island,_Florida "Santa Rosa Island, Florida"), a barrier island in the Gulf of Mexico.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-76) The 2020 population of the CDP is 1,123, up from 638 at the 2010 census.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-77)

Immediately to its east is [Navarre Beach Marine Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre_Beach_Marine_Park "Navarre Beach Marine Park"), a former Florida [state park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_park "State park"). Immediately to its west is a portion of the [Gulf Islands National Seashore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Islands_National_Seashore "Gulf Islands National Seashore"), and farther west is the community of [Pensacola Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola_Beach,_Florida "Pensacola Beach, Florida").

#### Recent history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Recent history")]

In 2006, a "beach re-nourishment" project was begun, restoring sand lost due to the hurricanes of 2004 and 2005. This project eventually added approximately 200 feet (61 m) of sand and a 14-foot (4.3 m) high berm to the Gulf side of Santa Rosa Island for the entire length of Navarre Beach. The project was completed in December 2006. Another round of beach re-nourishment was completed in 2016.

### Population estimates

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Population estimates")]

Navarre is a large community. Post-2020 estimates place the population as high as 43,540.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:26-7) If the town of Navarre was to be [incorporated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_corporation "Municipal corporation") it would be the largest city between [Pensacola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola "Pensacola") and [Tallahassee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallahassee "Tallahassee") (based on population).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:3-10)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:23-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-83) This is a major increase from just 40 years ago, when the population was hovering around 1,500.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:3-10)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:15-84)

## Arts and culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Arts and culture")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/NavarreBeachSignSpring.jpeg/250px-NavarreBeachSignSpring.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NavarreBeachSignSpring.jpeg)

The old Navarre Beach sign in the spring time

Tourism has increased in the Navarre area since 2010.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:12-85)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:9-31)

Local attractions include [Emerald Coast Wildlife Refuge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emerald_Coast_Wildlife_Refuge "Emerald Coast Wildlife Refuge"), Navarre Beach Marine Science Station, [Navarre Beach Sea Turtle Conservation Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre_Beach_Sea_Turtle_Conservation_Center "Navarre Beach Sea Turtle Conservation Center"), Sandspur Wildlife Sanctuary, and the Navarre Beach Marine Life Sanctuary.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-88)

The [Navarre Beach Fishing Pier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre_Beach_Fishing_Pier "Navarre Beach Fishing Pier") is 1,545 feet (471 m), and is the longest fishing pier on the Gulf of Mexico and in the state of Florida.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-89)

Public library services are provided by the [Santa Rosa County Library System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County_Library_System "Santa Rosa County Library System") through the [Navarre Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre_Library "Navarre Library").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-91)

## Parks and recreation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Parks and recreation")]

Parks and recreational facilities include [Navarre Beach Marine Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre_Beach_Marine_Park "Navarre Beach Marine Park"), Navarre Sports Complex, and Navarre Park, which features a playground, basketball courts, and picnic pavilions.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-92)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Education")]

Education in Navarre is administrated by the [Santa Rosa County School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County_School_District "Santa Rosa County School District"). Schools serving the Navarre community are:[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-93)

*   [Navarre High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre_High_School "Navarre High School")[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-94)
*   Holley-Navarre Middle School
*   Holley-Navarre Intermediate School
*   Holley-Navarre Primary School
*   Woodlawn Beach Middle School
*   West Navarre Primary School
*   West Navarre Intermediate School
*   East Bay K-8 School

## Infrastructure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Infrastructure")]

### Highways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Highways")]

*   [U.S. Route 98](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_98 "U.S. Route 98") (Navarre Parkway)
*   [Florida State Road 87](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Road_87 "Florida State Road 87")

### Airports

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Airports")]

Navarre doesn't have a dedicated commercially served airport. Instead, it is largely served by [Pensacola International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola_International_Airport "Pensacola International Airport") (about 25 miles west in [Pensacola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola,_Florida "Pensacola, Florida")) and [Destin–Fort Walton Beach Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destin%E2%80%93Fort_Walton_Beach_Airport "Destin–Fort Walton Beach Airport") (about 30 miles east in [Valparaiso, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valparaiso,_Florida "Valparaiso, Florida")).

[Fort Walton Beach Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Walton_Beach_Airport "Fort Walton Beach Airport") is a local general aviation airport.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:21-95)

[Naval Outlying Landing Field Holley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Outlying_Landing_Field_Holley "Naval Outlying Landing Field Holley"), previously a military airfield, has been converted to a solar field operated by [Gulf Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Power "Gulf Power") and the [United States Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-96)

### Public transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Navarre,_Florida&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Public transportation")]

Navarre has limited public transportation, despite some public calls for it.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-:26-7)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-97) Navarre does receive service from Santa Rosa Transportation, which provides some limited on-demand accessibility service from the town.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navarre,_Florida#cite_note-98)
